sec: Saline-unresponsive alkalosis: ECF volume expansion · p824

items.q: ECF volume expansion causes metabolic alkalosis that is:
opts: Saline unresponsive, with a normal urine Cl⁻ > 40 mEq/L
Saline responsive, with a urine Cl⁻ < 25 mEq/L
Saline unresponsive, with a urine Cl⁻ < 10 mEq/L
Saline responsive, with a high urine chloride
items.exp: ECF volume expansion = saline unresponsive metabolic alkalosis with a normal urine Cl⁻ (> 40 mEq/L). (Book p824)

items.q: Match the renin–aldosterone pattern to the major cause — 1) ↓Renin, ↑Aldosterone  2) ↑Renin, ↑Aldosterone  3) ↓Renin, ↓Aldosterone … A) Liddle syndrome — gain-of-function ENaC mutation  B) Primary hyperaldosteronism  C) Renal artery stenosis
items.exp: Major causes by pattern: ↓renin with ↑aldosterone = primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome); ↑renin with ↑aldosterone = RAS and renin-secreting tumours; ↓renin with ↓aldosterone = Liddle syndrome. (Book p824)

opts: A gain-of-function mutation of ENaC with ↓renin and ↓aldosterone
A loss-of-function mutation of ENaC with ↑renin and ↑aldosterone
A cortisol excess state with ↓renin and ↑aldosterone
An ACTH-driven aldosterone excess with ↑renin
items.exp: Liddle syndrome = gain of function mutation of ENaC, giving ↓renin and ↓aldosterone with alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: A hypertensive patient has metabolic alkalosis, suppressed renin, high aldosterone and a normal urine chloride. Which printed cause fits?
opts: Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome)
Liddle syndrome
Renin-secreting tumour of the juxtaglomerular apparatus
Post-hypercapnic alkalosis after chronic CO₂ retention
items.exp: The ↓renin/↑aldosterone box is labelled primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome), a saline-unresponsive cause. (Book p824)

items.q: ‘Renal artery stenosis produces metabolic alkalosis with high renin and high aldosterone.’
opts: True — ↑renin with ↑aldosterone is the printed RAS pattern
False — RAS produces low renin with high aldosterone
False — RAS produces low renin with low aldosterone
True, but only when the urine chloride is below 25 mEq/L
items.exp: The ↑renin/↑aldosterone column lists RAS and renin-secreting tumours among the major causes of saline-unresponsive alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: All but one of these are printed as major causes of saline-unresponsive metabolic alkalosis. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Vomiting with nasogastric aspiration with a urine Cl⁻ of 12 mEq/L
Liddle syndrome
Primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome)
Renin-secreting tumour
items.exp: Vomiting/NG aspiration cell is a *saline-responsive* cause (ECF volume contraction); the ECF-volume-expansion major causes are Conn's syndrome, RAS/renin-secreting tumours and Liddle syndrome. (Book p824)
